elements.element: No liquidated damages are payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 7.7 now expressly provides that Customer shall pay Vendor “no liquidated damages.” No other supplied clause imposes liquidated damages on Customer.

elements.element: No penalties are payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 7.7 now expressly provides that Customer shall pay Vendor “no penalty.” No other supplied clause imposes a penalty on Customer.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee payable by Customer is capped at three months' fees.
elements.evidence: Section 9.4 imposes no early-termination fee: Customer owes only accrued Fees and receives a refund of post-termination prepaid Fees. The cap is therefore satisfied because no such fee is payable.

elements.element: The capped early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount payable by Customer.
elements.evidence: No early-termination fee or other liquidated amount is payable. Section 7.7 expressly negates liquidated damages, and Section 9.4 limits termination amounts to accrued Fees. Thus there is no competing liquidated amount.

result.reason: The redline eliminates the only stated liquidated-damages and penalty obligation while leaving the payment-dispute and termination provisions substantively unchanged. It therefore achieves the preferred position and, as a more Customer-favorable outcome, also satisfies the fallback. The operative result is clear, though retaining the now-superfluous late-payment trigger and using the awkward phrase “shall pay Vendor no liquidated damages and no penalty” is lower-quality drafting than deleting Section 7.7 entirely or stating a general prohibition.
